slides.title: The one idea

content_blocks.block_data: Choosing is harder than generating, and it is where most student projects quietly fail.

slides.speaker_notes: Say it once. Do not elaborate on the slide — elaborate out loud.

slides.title: Why it matters

block_data.lead: You now have more ideas than time
block_data.body: Four sessions of material. That is the good problem.

block_data.lead: Three questions, in order: can the owner actuall
block_data.body: y do this? Can they start this month? With what they already have?

slides.speaker_notes: Four beats across two slides. Fifteen minutes for all of it.

slides.title: What to do with it

block_data.lead: An idea that fails any of the three is not a bad
block_data.body: idea — it is a later idea. Write it down and set it aside.
From here to Session 15 you are developing one idea, not keeping five alive.

slides.title: Today you will

content_blocks.block_data: Choose the single idea you will carry to the end of the semester, and write the case for it in five sentences.

slides.speaker_notes: Leave this slide up for the whole making phase.

slides.title: To close

block_data.head: Pitch
block_data.body: Three minutes. The person, the stuck, the idea, the picture, the ask.

block_data.head: Critique
block_data.body: I like… / I wish… / What if… — the idea, never the person.

block_data.head: Idea log
block_data.body: One page. Silent. Box 4 is the one you read again in week 15.

slides.speaker_notes: If time runs short, cut the input — never the pitch. The pitch is how CO 109.2 is attained.
